title: O Thou Who Cloth'st Thyself Complete
description: O Thou Who Cloth'st Thyself Complete in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns of the Greek Church (Edinburgh and London, 1900).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Thou who cloth'st Thy-self com-plete With light as with a gar-ment fair, Thou bor'st the cru-el, vul-gar stare, Un-robed be-fore the judg-ment seat.

lines: O Thou who cloth'st Thyself complete
With light as with a garment fair,
Thou bor'st the cruel, vulgar stare,
Thou gav'st the hand its subtle power,
But with the hand, O Lord of grace,
They smote Thee in that evil hour.
They nailed the Lord of Glory high,
And while He hung in awful pain,
The temple veil was rent in twain,
The sun refused to see Him die.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Greek Church (1900)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Greek Church; set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
